lead: Born by accident on a boat in the Grao of Gandia, fideuà is paella’s seafaring cousin: same technique, same fire, same ritual. But with noodles instead of rice and the Mediterranean in every bite.

Fideuà is not a paella with noodles: it is a dish with its own identity. The technique is similar — sofrito, toasting, fumet, rest — but the noodle absorbs the broth differently from rice, creating a denser texture and a concentrated flavour that is the hallmark of this seafaring dish. The word fideuà comes from the Valencian fideuada, “a large quantity of noodles”, which in turn comes from the Hispano-Arabic fidaws.

In Valencia there are versions for every taste: the classic seafood one, the senyoret one with cleaned seafood, the black one with squid ink, the huerta one with artichokes and snails, and even the lobster one or the duck and boletus one. Homemade alioli — never from a jar — is the essential accompaniment of any fideuà worthy of the name.

items.title: Traditional Fideuà of Gandia
items.subtitle: The original · Mediterranean seafood · Rockfish fumet · No. 3 or No. 4 noodle
items.body: The fideuà of Gandia is the original recipe, the one that came out of that boat in the Grao more than a century ago. Its ingredients are few and of top quality: firm-fleshed monkfish, cuttlefish or squid, prawns and langoustines over a concentrated, aromatic fumet of morralla — rockfish stock. The noodles are No. 3 or No. 4, thick and short. The secret lies in the sofrito of garlic, tomato and paprika, the prior toasting of the noodle in that same oil — which boosts the flavour of the wheat — and the exact point of cooking. It is always served with homemade alioli on the side, so that each diner mixes it to taste. The International Fideuà Competition of Gandia — since 1974 — is the world benchmark for this recipe.

items.title: Fideuà del Senyoret
items.subtitle: Seafood already peeled · No shells · The most comfortable · Valencian red prawn
items.body: Fideuà del senyoret — the young gentleman’s — is the most elegant and comfortable version to eat: all the seafood arrives at the table already peeled and cleaned, with no shells or work. The same concept as arroz del senyoret but with noodles. The Valencian red prawn, the cleaned clams and the boneless monkfish are built straight into the noodle, so that each bite combines toasted pasta with a piece of already-prepared seafood. The fumet, made with the heads and shells of that same seafood, concentrates all the flavour of the sea. In Valencia it is one of the most ordered in the restaurants of the historic centre and the Marina area. Casa BALDO 1915 makes it with red prawn and it is one of the most acclaimed in the city.

items.title: Black Fideuà
items.subtitle: Squid ink · Colour and intense flavour of the sea · Alioli essential
items.body: Black fideuà is the most visually spectacular version and one of the tastiest. Squid ink — added to the fumet or directly to the sofrito — dyes the noodles an intense black and adds a briny, marine, deep flavour that has no equal. It is made with squid or cuttlefish, prawns and sometimes baby squid, and the thick white alioli over the black base creates an extraordinary visual and taste contrast. The restaurant Puerta del Mar in Valencia has gone viral on social media with its black fideuà with grated prawns. It is a dish that wins over anyone who tries it for the first time and makes a regular of anyone who comes back.

items.title: Huerta Fideuà and Creative Variations
items.subtitle: Artichokes · Snails · Duck · Boletus · Fideuà beyond the sea
items.body: Valencia does not stop at the sea. Fideuà has evolved towards huerta and mountain versions that incorporate the most authentic products of the Valencian pantry. The artichoke and snail one — very popular in restaurants of the historic centre such as Pelayo Gastro Trinquet — recovers the flavour of the land. The duck and mushroom one combines game meats with the texture of the toasted noodle. The vegetable and boletus one from Masusa Paella Bar is one of the few vegetarian options in the genre. And the lobster fideuà — which appears on the menu of Casa BALDO 1915 — is the most festive and generous version. The basic technique is always the same: sofrito, toasted noodle, stock and the exact point.

items.title: The homemade fumet
items.body: With prawn heads, white fish bones and vegetables. Keep it hot before adding it

items.title: Toast the noodle
items.body: Sauté the noodles in the sofrito for 1 min before the stock — it activates the aromas of the wheat

items.title: Stir with judgement
items.body: Unlike rice, the noodle needs gentle movement so it does not stick or clump together

items.title: 3.5:1 proportion
items.body: 3.5 parts of fumet for every part of No. 4 noodle — adjust according to the heat

items.title: The subtle socarrat
items.body: Turn the heat up for 1 minute at the end to create the golden crust on the base

items.title: Rest 5 minutes
items.body: Turn off the heat and let it rest covered with a cloth before serving with alioli

items.title: Pelayo Gastro Trinquet
items.body: Set in the legendary Cathedral of Valencian Pilota, head chef Chimo Faubell makes the fideuà to order. The chicken and artichoke one cannot be missing from its set menu.
facts: Chicken and artichoke fideuà · 25 min preparation

items.title: Casa BALDO 1915
items.body: In a century-old shop that evokes the Valencia of the 50s. Head chef Jorge Parra masters all the variations, including the innovative fideuà of aged picanha tataki.
facts: Senyoret fideuà with red prawn · Lobster fideuà

items.title: Vaqueta Gastro Mercat
items.body: Next to the Mercat Central, Félix Escoto signs signature fideuàs with seasonal produce. The Iberian presa with boletus one surprises even the greatest purists of the seafaring genre.
facts: Snail and artichoke fideuà · Bluefin tuna tartare fideuà

items.title: Alquería del Pou
items.body: 500 m from the CAC, in a restored alquería with views of the huerta. Founded by Rafa Soler Orient, its seafood fideuà with fresh produce is one of the most highly rated in Valencia.

items.title: Puerta del Mar
items.body: The fumet of its black fideuà — viral on social media — is made with the freshest products from the fish market. A symbol of Mediterranean cooking in Valencia.
facts: Duck and mushroom fideuà · Black fideuà with grated prawns

items.title: El Paeller Valencià
items.body: The fumet broth is cooked over wood, which gives the noodles an extremely intense marine flavour. Squid, mussels, monkfish, peeled prawn and flying squid. Fideuà as it should be.
facts: Traditional fideuà cooked with wood-fired broth

blocks.title: What you should know before ordering fideuà in Valencia
items: Homemade alioli is not optional: it is an integral part of the dish — always ask for it and mix it in every bite to your taste
Authentic fideuà has a homemade rockfish fumet — be wary if the broth tastes like it came out of a packet
No. 3 or No. 4 noodle is the right one: neither too thin (it falls apart) nor too thick (it does not absorb the fumet)
Like paella, fideuà is a midday dish — Valencians do not eat fideuà for dinner; it is a dish of sun and sharing
The socarrat also exists in fideuà — the slightly toasted base is just as desirable as in paella
The International Fideuà Competition of Gandia is held annually — if you visit the Valencian coast in summer, don’t miss it
